claims.text: \paragraph{Relation to prior work.} DOMINO addresses subword alignment~\cite{pmlr-v235-beurer-kellner24a}; XGrammar uses local mask caching, context-dependent checks, and persistent stacks~\cite{MLSYS2025_5c20ca4b}. Outlines indexes vocabulary transitions~\cite{willard2023efficientguidedgenerationlarge}; SynCode develops formal syntactic guarantees~\cite{ugare2025syncode}; llguidance combines Earley parsing, lexing, and trie traversal~\cite{llguidance}. Lexer/parser products~\cite{pmlr-v267-park25l} and GPU-oriented token precompilation~\cite{pmlr-v306-hua26b} further develop this systems design space. Our bounds account for the operations represented by those techniques rather than compare model throughput.

The closest upper-bound predecessor is Parser Stack Classification (PSC)~\cite{li2026efficientgrammarconstraineddecodingparser}, whose regular classifier is executed by an $O(h)$ stack scan in Algorithm~2. VIABLE maintains reverse classifier annotations incrementally. Regularity, reversal, subset construction, and block tabulation are established automata tools; the result here is their explicit query/update/compilation accounting for exact completion masks. Its significance is the separation of query latency from committed parsing, rather than a new regularity theorem.

On the lower-bound side, Bringmann, Gr\o nlund, K\"unnemann, and Larsen formulate the NFA Acceptance hypothesis and show that it implies OMv~\cite{theoretics:13000}. Their fixed-word acceptance and colored-walk formulations provide important complexity context. Gibney and Thankachan study preprocessing a text for subsequent regular-expression queries~\cite{Gibney_2021}. Our static object is the grammar, the online object is appended text, and the answer is a candidate-completion bit along prefixes kept live by a universal branch. These distinctions specify the transfer that the proof must establish; regular-language OMv hardness alone is already part of the surrounding literature.

Online CFL recognition has a different predicate: it reports membership of each observed prefix. Dudek and Gawrychowski give an upper bound using OMv methods~\cite{dudek_et_al:LIPIcs.CPM.2024.13}. Earlier online Turing-machine lower bounds~\cite{Gallaire_1969}, sliding-window bounds with deletion~\cite{ganardi_et_al:LIPIcs.FSTTCS.2022.38}, and offline parsing barriers~\cite{Lee:02a,Abboud_2015} concern different machines, updates, or outputs. The reduction below fixes these choices directly. Type-constrained generation~\cite{M_ndler_2025} and semantic realizability~\cite{Nagy_2026} motivate the auxiliary typed-completion result in Section~\ref{sec:types}.

\begin{lemma}[Regular constrained futures]\label{lem:regular} For a normalized pushdown machine and a regular input language $R$, the configurations that can consume a word in $R$ and accept after EOF form an effectively constructible regular set. \end{lemma} \begin{proof} Take the product with an automaton for $R$, updating its state on consuming transitions. Permit EOF only at an accepting $R$ state. A regular target after EOF is represented by an NFA reading stacks top to bottom, with product controls as initial states and separate internal target states. Initially no edge enters a control state. For each pushdown rule $(p,A)\longrightarrow(q,\beta)$, $|\beta|\le2$, add $p\xrightarrow A u$ whenever a current path $q\xrightarrow\beta u$ exists. This saturation adds edges but no states, and terminates in polynomial time~\cite{10.1007/3-540-63141-0_10}.

\begin{proof}[Lower bounds in Theorem~\ref{thm:omv}] Use the standard polynomial-preprocessing consequence of OMv~\cite{Henzinger_2015}; its precise form is Theorem~2.2 of the full version, arXiv:1511.06773. Preprocess the grammar. On each revealed vector $v$, commit $v\#$, then one $a$ per row. After the $i$th $a$, output the mask's $?$ bit as $(Av)_i$. Commit $!$ after the last row. Only then request the next vector. The stream never commits $?$ and every actual prefix can extend to a universal block, including for an all-zero matrix.

Invoke the polynomial-space simple-type inhabitation procedure~\cite{Statman_1979,Švejdar2003} separately for each obligation, reusing its workspace, and test the finitely many partial-head alternatives sequentially. Each procedure receives polynomial-size input; the outer enumeration and contexts occupy polynomial space. This proves membership. For hardness, a closed type $A$ maps to empty context and empty prefix at target $A$. It is completable exactly when $A$ is inhabited, since every inhabited simple type has a long normal inhabitant. The same empty-prefix reduction gives unrestricted-source hardness. \end{proof}

[Regular-family lower bounds]\label{thm:omv} Under OMv, for every $\epsilon>0$ there is no uniform exact engine with $\poly(g+D)$ preprocessing and amortized $O(n^{1/2-\epsilon})$ time per step on all right-linear grammars. This holds with an identity lexer, $M=D=6$, and $L=1$, on a family with $g=\Theta(m^2)$ and $n=\Theta(m^2)$. The same family admits $O(1+m/w)$ worst-case steps and $O(m^2)$ preprocessing and space.  With one polynomial preprocessing and $m$ independently initialized streams of horizon $n=\Theta(m)$, constant-time initialization, and $g=\Theta(n^2)$, the excluded bound is instead amortized $O(n^{1-\epsilon})$ per step.

[Explicit stack index]\label{thm:index} For a supplied deterministic presentation, a joint bottom-to-top configuration classifier with \[s=O\bigl(g(M+1)(D+L+1)\bigr)\] NFA states can be constructed in $\poly(g+D+L)$ time. Determinizing it yields a VIABLE index with preprocessing $\poly(g+D+L)+2^{O(s)}$ and static space \[O\bigl(\poly(g+D+L)+2^s(|\Gamma|+|Q|B)\bigr). \] On addressable instances, mask queries cost $O(B)$ worst-case, commits cost $O(|v_i|+r_i+1)$, and dynamic space is $O(1+W_t)$ words. Thus bounded-work presentations have $O(B+bL+b)$ worst-case steps, and linear-work presentations have total online time $O(tB+an+a+t)$.

[Block-tabulation tradeoff]\label{thm:blocks} Given the classifier of Theorem~\ref{thm:index}, choose $1\le b\le\min(s,w)$, let $k=\lceil s/b\rceil$ and $d=\lceil s/w\rceil$. Besides polynomial classifier construction, preprocessing time and static space are \begin{equation}\label{eq:tradeoff}  O\bigl(\poly(s+g+D)+2^b k(|\Gamma|d+|Q|B)\bigr). \end{equation} Mask queries cost $O(kB)$, a push costs $O(kd)$, and a pop costs $O(1)$. Committing token $i$ costs $O(|v_i|+(r_i+1)kd)$, with dynamic space $O((1+W_t)d)$. All bounds are worst-case for the specified operations.

[Regular constrained futures]\label{lem:regular} For a normalized pushdown machine and a regular input language $R$, the configurations that can consume a word in $R$ and accept after EOF form an effectively constructible regular set.

[Grammar size and query predicate]\label{lem:gadget} A right-linear grammar of size $O(m^2)$ for $K_A$ can be built in $O(m^2)$ time and padded to $\Theta(m^2)$. For $p\in B_m^*$, \begin{equation}\label{eq:probe}  \mask_{pv\#a^i}[?]=(Av)_i\qquad(1\le i\le m). \end{equation}

[Normal typed-prefix completion]\label{thm:types} Given $\Delta,A$ and a text prefix in this serialization, extendibility is PSPACE-complete in their combined size. Empty-prefix completion in unrestricted STLC source syntax is PSPACE-hard.
